name: GNU Coreutils
summary: A family of Unix command-line utilities organized around common option, operand, stream, and exit-status conventions, with a documented multi-call program as an additional packaging form.

features.name: Common option and operand contract
features.description: The Coreutils manual documents common option handling, option terminators, operands such as standard input represented by '-', and shared --help and --version conventions across the utility family, with documented command-specific exceptions.
benefits: Makes utilities predictable to invoke individually and from scripts
Allows generic command-line tooling to target a family of programs
costs: Common conventions still have command-specific exceptions

features.name: Stream and status composition
features.description: The documented utilities operate on files, standard input, and standard output, and nearly every invocation yields an integral exit status where zero generally indicates success and nonzero indicates failure.
benefits: Supports composition through shell pipelines, redirection, and scripts
Exposes a small process boundary for success and failure propagation
costs: Text and status interfaces do not express all semantic distinctions
Locale, filesystem, and platform behavior remain external dependencies

features.name: Multi-call program packaging
features.description: The official manual documents a coreutils multi-call program alongside the individual utility interfaces, showing that the utility family can also be packaged behind a shared executable boundary.
benefits: Can consolidate related utility entry points into one deployed program
Preserves the family-level command model while changing packaging
costs: Dispatch and packaging add another invocation mode to document and test
Shared packaging does not remove differences among utility semantics

mathematical_views.question: How can utilities be composed when their principal boundary is streams, operands, and an exit status?
assumptions: A command is modeled as a transformation from input streams and operands to output streams and status
Composition abstracts shell process creation, buffering, signals, and filesystem races
The model describes interface shape and does not imply that arbitrary utilities compose without semantic loss

mathematical_views.question: Which user-visible command interfaces can be preserved when a utility family moves between separate executables and a multi-call executable?
assumptions: The dispatch name selects a utility behavior within the multi-call program
The view compares invocation boundaries and does not claim binary or performance equivalence
Filesystem, environment, and platform effects are held constant for the comparison

costs: Shared conventions must accommodate historical and command-specific behavior

benefits: Simple boundaries for shell and script composition
costs: Structured semantics often require conventions outside the stream and status contract

benefits: Alternative deployment form for a related utility family
costs: Dispatch behavior and executable packaging increase operational variation
